newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares rise in healthy select trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares rise in healthy select trade.

text.p: Amman's bourse rose on Monday as strong demand emerged after healthy 1996 results of leading blue-chips were given a push by Middle East peace optimism and renewal of an annual oil deal with Iraq, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.12 percent to 153.40 points in turnover worth 707,391 dinars ($999,139).

Brokers cited improved investor sentiment with signs of progress in Middle East peace talks after an Israel-Palestinian deal over the West Bank town of Hebron along with news of Iraq's agreement to supply the kingdom's oil needs for 1997.
This helped boost some leading bluechips, including mining stock such as Arab Potash Company and leading Arab Bank, which announced in the last few days good 1996 results.
Brokers detected institutional buyers emerging on Monday in one of the more active days since the start last week of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan, when trading is usually weak.

"The market performed well with investors starting to look at results of companies, with some outside buying on some firms combined with the favourable political climate," said Ibrahim Odeh, a broker at al-Wataniyah for Financial Services.
Middle East Investment Bank, both the top price gainer and most heavily traded stock, gained 3.51 percent to 1.18 dinars in trade worth 91,103 dinars.

Dealers say interest in the bank, one of Jordan's smaller private banks, is helped by reports it is close to finalising a deal with a French banking group with a regional presence to acquire an equity stake in a planned capitalisation issue.
Arab Paper Converting and Trading was again among the handful of the market's good performers with a 3.39 percent rise to 1.22 dinars in trade worth 44,824 dinars.
Cigarette manufacturer International Tobacco rose 0.03 dinars to 1.30 dinars in trade worth 57,998 dinars.
Overall rising shares outnumbered falling shares by 15 to 11, with another 17 trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange fell 0.11 percent to 82.25 points.
